chunks: And from him, from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, sometimes we are tested with an eclipse after Maghrib but before the final Isha prayer. If we pray the eclipse prayer, we fear missing the obligatory [Isha] prayer.' He said, 'If you fear that, cut off your eclipse prayer, fulfill your obligatory prayer, then return to it.' I said, 'And if the eclipse is at the end of the night, and we pray the eclipse prayer but miss the night prayer [Tahajjud/Qiyam], which of the two do we begin with?' He said, 'Pray the eclipse prayer and fulfill the night prayer when you wake up in the morning.'

key_terms.الْمَغْرِب: Maghrib (the third of the five daily prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing eclipse prayer if it conflicts with the obligatory Isha prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy between the Sunnah eclipse prayer and obligatory prayers, emphasizing flexibility by allowing the interruption of the former to secure the latter. It further establishes the principle of making up missed voluntary night prayers (Qiyam) after sunrise if they are displaced by the eclipse, reflecting the Shia juristic view on balancing ritual obligations with celestial phenomena. This ruling underscores the practical adaptability of Shia fiqh in managing overlapping worship times without compromising the validity of either act.
